- When sentiment turns bullish sharply (positive change > 0.5) and news volume spikes, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- After a strong price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% of spike magnitude from forecast 2–4 days later.
- If sentiment is consistently bearish (avg sentiment < 0.3) and price is trending down, model under-forecasts; add 2–5% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- When sentiment changes direction abruptly (e.g., from +0.5 to -0.5), model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- High news volume with low sentiment (e.g., news > 2.0, sentiment < 0.5) correlates with underperformance; model under-forecasts; add 3–7% to forecast to compensate.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending sideways, model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 2–5% to match mean reversion.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 3–6% to reflect sentiment misalignment.
